body: Dameon Pierce scored thirteen for CHANE GANG, while reserve running backs TreVeyon Henderson and Keaton Mitchell supplied 2.5 and 0.4. Pierce’s 10.5-point advantage over Henderson helped support the receiving production in a 15.92-point win. A useful start on the actual results, not a claim that the choice was obvious before kickoff.

Trevor Lawrence’s 28.34 remained on the bench while Matthew Stafford supplied 16.88. The 11.46-point difference exceeds Tolbert’s Cookies’ 1.48-point loss to Scrump; that single substitution produces a 100.24–90.26 win. This is a decisive same-position retrospective, not proof that Greg ignored information available before lock.
sunday-crew.title: Start / Sit of the Week

body: Andrew has finally arranged for the standings to agree with him, although only as far as three and three. A Stroke of Bad Luck beat ZAYWATCH 100.52–97.14, leaving both managers with the same record. Our preview noted that Andrew had scored more while Sandy had won more. The direct meeting has resolved the discrepancy by removing Sandy's advantage rather than making either season especially comfortable.

Kenneth Walker supplied 28.9, nearly as much as Andrew's other two starting running backs combined with all three starting receivers. Kirk Cousins added 21.52. This was not an afternoon of universal distinction. MarShawn Lloyd contributed one; Pat Freiermuth supplied 2.1. Andrew won with several members of the party apparently attending in an advisory capacity.

Sandy's response was less concentrated. Jordan Love, Germie Bernard and George Kittle all reached fifteen, and Bernard's 20.2 gave ZAYWATCH a substantial receiving contribution. It simply did not produce the last 3.38. None of Sandy’s recorded bench players scored. There is no obvious selection to point at after the fact, no gratifying little substitution with which to rewrite the result. This is not evidence of a winning alternative hidden underneath the result.

Sandy's three-game winning run ends; Andrew reaches level terms. There is no need to make this a settlement of their relative abilities, much less their histories. Andrew has something more useful than a persuasive explanation this morning: the victory itself. Sandy now has the explanation. The league does enjoy distributing the work.
sunday-crew.title: A more convenient kind of fairness

body: Joe’s J Bird posted Sunday Crew’s highest Week 6 score, 151.74, to beat Runit and reach three and three after three straight wins. Nipun moved to five and one, the league’s only one-loss record. Paul beat Ravi to join Runit and Greg at four and two. Andrew and Sandy now share three-and-three records; Cody and Drew each collected a second win. Drew’s 1.48-point escape against Greg was the closest finish, one of two games decided by fewer than four.
sunday-crew.title: Nipun alone at five and one; Joe changes the front of the race

body: Patrick's bench contains Lamar Jackson and Saquon Barkley. Their names look like an answer until you reach the Week 6 points column, where both have zero. The distinction matters. Rhamondre – A Cautionary Tale lost 100.88–88.52 to Nipun, and the familiar exercise of finding the victory Patrick failed to select produces nothing among his recorded reserves. A prestigious bench is not necessarily usable inventory.

The preview gave Patrick urgency and Nipun patience. The completed lineup gives those abstractions a less flattering physical form. Patrick started Rhamondre Stevenson and Kenny Gainwell for a combined 6.5. DeMario Douglas led his offensive players with 16.1, while the kicker and defense supplied another 23.2 between them. Those contributions kept the result respectable without solving the shortage at running back.

Nipun did not need another extraordinary Christian Watson week. C.J. Stroud supplied 23.98; four other offensive starters reached double figures. Derrick Henry's 4.5 and Harold Fannin's 1.4 were survivable because the rest of the lineup kept producing useful amounts. Quentin Johnston, the only scoring player on the recorded bench, would not have improved any of Nipun's starting receiver totals.

The resulting positions are five and one for Nipun, one and five for Patrick. Our warning against emergency tinkering survives, but it needs a qualification: sometimes the problem is not excessive movement. Sometimes the roster has very little that can move. Patrick does not need to prove that his famous players are famous. He needs a Sunday on which their names come with numbers.
sunday-crew.title: The savings account has a password

body: Paul and Ravi arrived separated by less than three season points. They left separated by 35.34 on the week, which feels excessive for two people who had spent five Sundays establishing how much they had in common. Croatian Sensation won 131.30–95.96. The resemblance has been discontinued, and Paul gets to keep the more flattering photograph.

It was not his receivers who broke the symmetry. Davante Adams, A.J. Brown and Rome Odunze combined for fifteen, an unusually expensive-looking way to obtain fifteen. James Cook and D'Andre Swift supplied 43.8 at running back. Drake Maye added 25.8, and the Chiefs defense contributed 19.6. Paul could have placed the three receivers in a separate, much less successful fantasy league and still had most of his afternoon intact.

Ravi's receivers were considerably more cooperative. Drake London, CeeDee Lamb and Khalil Shakir all reached double figures, with DeVonta Smith adding seventeen in the flex. Then the lineup wandered elsewhere: Justin Herbert finished below ten, Mark Andrews below one, and neither starting running back reached double digits. It is mildly offensive to have the better receiving afternoon and lose this decisively. It is also what the other positions are for.

Paul reaches four and two; Ravi drops to three and three. There is no single benched savior to rescue Ravi's result, and Paul's win does not make every choice immaculate: Hunter Henry outscored Travis Kelce from the bench. But our preview anticipated competing explanations from two nearly identical teams. Paul can now decline the discussion. His running backs have already supplied rather more separation than good manners require.
sunday-crew.title: The resemblance was temporary

body: Matt had 26.96 from Tyler Shough on the bench and 11.48 from Patrick Mahomes in the lineup. There is a familiar little tragedy available here, until the arithmetic interferes: swapping the quarterbacks would still have left Forte inch Ditka 0.44 behind Cody. Even the imaginary rescue needed somebody to come back with a second vehicle.

CHANE GANG won 112.90–96.98. Our preview framed this as two struggling teams meeting without the consolation of a glamorous opponent. Cody's actual lineup made the more interesting distinction. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Luther Burden, Tet McMillan and flex receiver Carnell Tate supplied 62.5 between them. Four separate receiving spots, all in double figures. A zero from Juwan Johnson at tight end did not swallow the afternoon because the receivers kept handing something back.

Matt had substantial help from Jonathan Taylor and Isaiah Likely, who combined for forty-one. Beyond that, the contribution became uneven. Blake Corum's thirteen on the bench exceeded Omarion Hampton's 5.9 by 7.1, a real same-position improvement but not enough by itself to change the result. The two substitutions together would reverse it. That is a retrospective calculation, not evidence that either choice was obvious before kickoff.

Both managers are now two and four. Cody has another win to work from; Matt has a quarterback question that was already present in last week's coverage. The distinction matters more than a verdict on Mahomes from one afternoon. We keep looking for the one decision that explains an entire loss. This one required two. Cody, mercifully, can spend the morning with the lineup that actually played.
sunday-crew.title: Forty-four hundredths of a rescue

body: Joe did not merely find enough ceiling to trouble Runit. J Bird scored 151.74, the highest total in Sunday Crew, and beat RBs are Overrated by 58.94. Our preview asked whether Joe could make the favorite react. There is a point at which react becomes an unnecessarily ambitious assignment. Runit finished at 92.80.

Malik Nabers and Christian McCaffrey supplied 55.7. That pair almost covered the entire winning margin, but the separation was not confined to two stars: Colston Loveland scored 15.5, Tyler Bass seventeen and the Steelers defense 14.6. Across quarterback, running back, receiver, tight end, kicker and defense, Joe had a starter above twelve. This was ceiling distributed across positions, not one eruption concealing a lineup that otherwise failed.

The bench makes the outcome stranger without improving the process verdict. Tre Tucker scored 26.2 while Denzel Boston supplied two in the flex. That is a 24.2-point receiving substitution Joe could have benefited from retrospectively. It does not mean he should have known it beforehand, and it certainly does not turn a league-leading afternoon into an instructional failure. Winning comfortably is allowed to coexist with points left unused.

Runit had improvements available too, including RJ Harvey over Bucky Irving and Keon Coleman over Michael Wilson. Neither comes remotely close to erasing the margin by itself. Joe reaches three and three after opening with three losses; Runit is four and two. Three straight wins now support Joe's recovery. The next test is repeating useful production, not demanding another one fifty. He has already demonstrated that an imperfect lineup can be a very strong one.
sunday-crew.title: The ceiling was already in the lineup

body: Drew collected his second win in a game in which he was not especially good. He entered the week leading Sunday Crew in scoring with a single victory. Scrump beat Tolbert's Cookies 90.26–88.78. Nine other teams scored more than Drew. The schedule, having spent September refusing to recognize his work, has now approved a much weaker application.

Matthew Golden supplied 21.4, Brock Purdy 17.36 and DK Metcalf 14.8. Elsewhere, Scrump did enough damage to itself to keep the matter open: Cam Skattebo finished with zero, Courtland Sutton with 2.9, and the kicker with two. None of the recorded reserves offered the sort of replacement that would turn this into a story about Drew overlooking a great performance. He won with the points actually available in his selected lineup, which is refreshing chiefly because he previously kept losing with considerably more.

Greg's bench presents a different problem. Trevor Lawrence outscored Matthew Stafford by 11.46. Bhayshul Tuten outscored both starting running backs, and Alvin Kamara exceeded both as well. Any one of several straightforward same-position changes would have erased a 1.48-point defeat. That does not establish which choice was justified before kickoff. It does establish that this particular loss has a more practical investigation available than an appeal to cosmic fairness.

Drew is two and four. Greg is four and two after losing consecutive games. Our preview offered Drew another chance to prove the standings wrong. Instead, the standings have finally done him a favor. He need not return it out of intellectual consistency. The championship was not awarded for maintaining a coherent complaint.
sunday-crew.title: Justice lowers its standards

body: Scrump scored 144.56 and lost in Week 5. It scored 90.26 and won in Week 6. Nine Sunday Crew teams outscored Drew this time; Greg was not one of them. The defending champion’s two-and-four record is better by one win, while his argument about the schedule has become considerably less tidy.

Tre Tucker’s 26.2 on the bench exceeded Denzel Boston’s two in the flex by 24.2. J Bird nevertheless posted 151.74, Sunday Crew’s highest score, and won by 58.94. The extra points matter for reviewing the selection. They do not invalidate the production already in the lineup.

Tyler Shough outscored starting quarterback Patrick Mahomes by 15.48. Forte inch Ditka lost by 15.92. The most obvious alternative therefore ends 0.44 short. Blake Corum over Omarion Hampton would supply a further 7.1, but needing two hindsight substitutions is not the same as finding one neglected winning button.

Croatian Sensation’s three starting receivers combined for fifteen, fewer than Ravi’s DeVonta Smith alone. James Cook and D’Andre Swift supplied 43.8, Drake Maye 25.8 and the Chiefs defense 19.6. Paul won by 35.34 despite losing the more photogenic comparison.

Kenneth Walker’s 28.9 helped A Stroke of Bad Luck beat ZAYWATCH by 3.38. Both teams now stand at three and three. Sandy’s three-game winning run is over; Andrew has converted a prior advantage in season scoring into a rather more convenient direct result.

Every recorded reserve on Patrick’s Week 6 roster scored zero. The starting running backs supplied 6.5 combined, and Rhamondre lost by 12.36. Nipun is five and one; Patrick is one and five. Whatever the future value of those bench names, none supplied an actual Week 6 alternative.
sunday-crew.title: Autopsy

body: Cody won 91.70–91.52 with 7.6 from his starting running backs. Carnell Tate and Emeka Egbuka supplied 30.3 from the two flex spots. Bryan left Kyle Pitts’s 20.5 on the bench in favor of Tyler Higbee’s 2.2; that hindsight gap dwarfs the 0.18 margin. The victory does not repair Cody’s running-back problem. It does give him the pleasant option of discussing it from 4–2.

The preview emphasized a possible flex decision. Tyler Shough and Christian McCaffrey supplied 53.16 for Sandy, and the Chiefs defense added 15. Even exchanging Alan’s quarterback and one running back for their higher-scoring bench alternatives leaves him 12.28 behind. McConkey Kong is 3–3; Gimothy Blossoms is 2–4. This was not a narrow game hiding inside a poor selection.

Extremely Tight Ends won 98.06–85.50 while Harold Fannin Jr. supplied 1.4. James Cook and DeMario Douglas combined for 38.9. Jason’s Bears falls to 3–3; Pete is 4–2 and fourth. The tight end did not have to do very much. The name still gets printed above eight other teams.

Ordway won 137.80–136.82, the two highest scores of DOGE’s week. Jason now has 784.52 season points and a 5–1 record; Corey has 770.20 and is 2–4. Isaiah Likely delivered 20.9 from a flex spot. Corey’s two-tight-end arrangement continues to work rather better than his schedule. Fourteen points of cumulative scoring separate three wins.

Andrew beat Bennett 109.48–83.72 behind Kenneth Walker’s 28.9. Tucker’s 26.2 stayed on Bennett’s bench; putting him into Lloyd’s one-point flex slot would still leave Tranimal 0.56 short. Both brothers are 4–2. Bennett retains the higher place on season points. Andrew has the actual result, which requires considerably less explanation.

Bo Nix scored 4.48, but Matthew Golden and Colston Loveland supplied 34.9 as Patrick won 110.08–99.94. Moe’s quarterback and running-back production offered things to keep, not a second win. Even Diggs for Wicks would leave him 0.14 short. Patrick moves to 2–4; Moe is 1–5. Improvement has arrived at both teams. The standings recognize only one visit.
doge.title: Autopsy

body: Patrick put Matthew Golden in a flex spot and got 19.4 in a 10.14-point win over Moe. Michael Wilson, a same-position bench option, scored 5.2. Replacing Golden with Wilson would have turned the win into a 4.06-point loss. The quarterback supplied only 4.48; this is where Nix in 5 found room to survive. Retrospective credit for the result, not a claim that the choice was obvious before lock.

Bryan started Tyler Higbee for 2.2 while Kyle Pitts scored 20.5 on the bench. In a 0.18-point loss, the 18.3-point tight-end gap is difficult to look past. Pitts in that slot produces a 109.82–91.70 hypothetical win. This is completed-week arithmetic, not evidence about availability, information or reasonable expectations before lock.
doge.title: Start Sit

body: Cody has won another game without meaningfully weakening the case against his team. Caleb’s Elite Touch Rate beat T. Ocellus 91.70–91.52. Bryan lost by eighteen hundredths of a point, a margin so small that rounding becomes an act of political favoritism.

The preview asked whether Cody could keep winning with modest production. Apparently the answer is yes, provided we retain enough decimal places. His starting running backs supplied 7.6 points between them. Last week’s recap identified that position as a problem; this week’s victory has not offered a rebuttal. Carnell Tate and Emeka Egbuka supplied 30.3 from the two flex spots, doing useful work while the running backs explored the minimum contribution compatible with employment.

Bryan had three substantial performances: Kirk Cousins, Jonathan Taylor and Germie Bernard each cleared twenty. He also started Tyler Higbee for 2.2 while Kyle Pitts scored 20.5 on the bench. That is an 18.3-point same-position difference in a game decided by 0.18. It does not tell us what Bryan reasonably knew before lock. It does tell us why this particular defeat will resist being filed under general misfortune.

Cody is now 4–2 with fewer season points than ten of the league’s twelve teams. Bryan is 2–4. The standings are not obliged to reward our preferred interpretation of events, which is part of their charm and most of their cruelty. Cody need not win the argument about how good his team is. At present, he is winning something much more useful.
doge.title: The second decimal is doing a lot of work

body: Patrick has won his second game, although Bo Nix did relatively little to advance the franchise bearing his name. Nix supplied 4.48 in a 110.08–99.94 victory over De’Coldest Hassan. There is nothing disqualifying about this. Institutions often carry the name of someone whose current contribution is largely ceremonial.

Matthew Golden scored 19.4 from a flex spot, Colston Loveland 15.5 at tight end, and the Bears defense added eleven. Patrick’s remaining lineup supplied enough to make the quarterback’s afternoon survivable. This is more useful than the general promise of a turnaround: specific positions performed the work while the most visible position did not. Nix in 5 moves to 2–4 without requiring us to describe the entire roster as suddenly cured.

Moe had the more productive quarterback. Jordan Love supplied 21.24, and his starting running backs combined for 19.5, a substantial improvement on the five noted in last week’s recap. There is genuine progress here. It simply remains less progress than the opponent. Stefon Diggs’s 13.4 stayed on the bench while Dontayvion Wicks scored 3.4; that same-position swap would still leave Moe 0.14 short. An exceptionally efficient way to make even hindsight feel inadequate.

The preview placed both men in the explanation business at 1–4. One now has a win; the other has a better account of why a win might be possible. We should not confuse those developments, but neither should we pretend the second is worthless. Moe is 1–5 with a functional quarterback and more running-back production. Patrick has the more immediate luxury. He can spend this week discussing what needs improving without first explaining why nothing ever does.
doge.title: The turnaround arrives without its namesake

body: Our preview suggested one useful flex decision could define Alan and Sandy’s week. Sandy won 122.16–96.14, and his flex players did beat Alan’s by 2.2 points. That is not where the other twenty-four points came from. The narrow-game premise needs retiring before it acquires a second career as analysis.

Tyler Shough and Christian McCaffrey supplied 53.16 for McConkey Kong. Alan’s quarterback and two running backs combined for 39.14. Add Sandy’s fifteen from the Chiefs defense against Alan’s two from Jacksonville and the shape of the result becomes considerably less mysterious. This was production at several positions, not one inspired little switch secretly running the whole afternoon.

There is a tempting bench correction for Gimothy Blossoms: C.J. Stroud scored 25.98 to Bryce Young’s 19.84, and Alvin Kamara’s 13.9 exceeded Bijan Robinson’s 6.3. Those two same-position substitutions together recover 13.74. Alan still loses by 12.28. Hindsight has been granted the starting quarterback and a running back, and it still cannot win the game. That should constrain the lecture about lineup discipline.

Sandy returns to 3–3 after last week’s loss, when Shough supplied fewer than two points. One week later the same quarterback clears twenty-six. That does not make the earlier result a sensible forecast, or this one a permanent new floor. It does give McConkey Kong a win that is more substantial than the close-call story we prepared. Alan falls to 2–4. There are decisions to review, but not every defeat contains a single button the manager forgot to press.
doge.title: The flex spot was not the whole story

body: Pete appears to have misunderstood which part of Extremely Tight Ends required exaggerating. The record is 4–2. The tight end scored 1.4. Harold Fannin Jr. was the only starter below three, which seems an unusually restrained interpretation of extremely.

James Cook supplied 22.8 and DeMario Douglas added 16.1 from a flex spot in the 98.06–85.50 win over RFK Jr’s Bears. I made the preview about whether two ridiculous names could support a serious contest. Pete has supplied the more interesting distinction: the thing everybody remembers about a team need not be the thing helping it win. We are discussing the tight end because Pete has practically instructed us to. Douglas, whose surname has not been worked into an innuendo, was rather more useful.

Jason got thirteen each from Blake Corum and Puka Nacua. Derrick Henry and Marvin Harrison Jr. combined for 9.4. Josh Allen supplied 18.3, but there was no enormous score available to make the quieter contributions disappear. The Bears fall to 3–3. Pete’s lineup also had an uncomfortable detail: Trevor Lawrence scored 28.34 on the bench, nearly ten more than Brock Purdy. Winning makes that considerably easier to scroll past.

There is a particular freedom in getting away with a name like this. Lose, and everyone can point to the 1.4. Win, and they are forced to put Extremely Tight Ends fourth in the standings. Fannin need not have done much. Pete has made the rest of the league type it.
doge.title: The name is doing the strenuous part

body: Corey produced the second-highest score in DOGE4 this week and received the same win total as the man who finished last. Unfortunately, he was playing the highest. Ordway and Son won 137.80–136.82. The preview asked why comparable production was buying Jason so much more success. The answer arrived with a margin of 0.98, which feels unnecessarily specific.

There was plenty worth keeping in El Niño Grande’s lineup. Bhayshul Tuten supplied 22.7. Isaiah Likely added 20.9 from a flex spot, another productive week for Corey’s two-tight-end arrangement. Jaxon Smith-Njigba contributed 19.4. This was not a good-looking total assembled around one impossible performance. Several positions worked, and the result still went elsewhere.

Jason, meanwhile, survived 0.9 from Mark Andrews and zero from Cam Skattebo. Drake Maye, Chuba Hubbard and D’Andre Swift combined for 66.4; Tyler Bass contributed seventeen. There is no need to invent a sophisticated management doctrine that explains why this lineup won by less than a point. It produced enough, distributed imperfectly, against the only other team that came close.

The cumulative figures now make the distinction brutal. Jason leads the league at 5–1 with 784.52 points. Corey is 2–4 with 770.20, second in scoring and eighth in the standings. Three games of separation in the win column have been purchased with 14.32 extra points across six weeks. Corey does not need to dismantle an offense that keeps supplying evidence in its favor. He needs a result. Unfortunately, the league does not sell those separately, and it has once again declined his offer to pay in points.
doge.title: A very expensive ninety-eight hundredths

body: Andrew has beaten his brother, and the family result comes with a small piece of arithmetic that makes it harder to dismiss. Jerruh’s World won 109.48–83.72. Bennett left Tre Tucker’s 26.2 on the bench. Move Tucker into MarShawn Lloyd’s one-point flex spot and Andrew still wins, by 0.56. Even the obvious alternate ending refuses to get Bennett home.

The preview made much of the brothers’ competing claims to the top of the league. Kenneth Walker supplied the more practical argument: 28.9 points for Andrew. Hunter Henry and Ryan Flournoy contributed another 26.3 between them. Andrew did this with a zero from Tyler Warren in the other flex spot, so nobody involved is being invited to submit the lineup as a model of human perfection.

For Tranimal, Malik Nabers scored 26.5 and DK Metcalf added 14.8. The two starting running backs combined for 14.1. Last week Bennett won comfortably behind running-back production; this week that part of the arrangement stopped doing enough. Tucker’s bench score deserves inspection, but it should not swallow the account of a team that finished more than twenty-five points behind.

Both brothers are now 4–2. Bennett remains narrowly ahead on season points, which is the sort of technical distinction a table is obliged to honor and a sibling is free to find unpersuasive. I cannot tell you what either man will say about this game. The result supplies sufficient material without fabricating the conversation. Andrew won the actual matchup, and he survives the most conspicuous one-player rewrite. Bennett can keep his place immediately above him in the standings. It has become a remarkably poor place to look down from.
doge.title: The family result survives the bench audit

body: Ordway and Son leads DOGE 4 at 5–1 after edging El Niño Grande 137.80–136.82. Corey had the second-highest score of the week and still fell to 2–4. Cody’s 91.70–91.52 win over Bryan required even less separation; he joins Andrew, Bennett and Pete at 4–2. Andrew beat his brother, Sandy returned to even, and Patrick earned his second win. Week 6 is final. The completed matchups stay in view; these are not Week 7 projections.
doge.title: Two decimals, very different seasons
